question: In a certain code language, "STONE" is written as "PQLKB." How will "CHAIR" be written in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ZEXFO.

GIVEN

• STONE → PQLKB; find the code of CHAIR.

SOLUTION

• Compare letter by letter: S → P, T → Q, O → L, N → K, E → B.

• Every letter moves 3 places backward in the alphabet (S−3 = P, T−3 = Q, O−3 = L, N−3 = K, E−3 = B).

• CHAIR: C−3 = Z (wrap-around), H−3 = E, A−3 = X (wrap-around), I−3 = F, R−3 = O.

• Code = ZEXFO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When the first letter of the code is exactly 3 steps away, check whether the same shift holds for the rest, then apply it with wrap-around (A−3 = X, B−3 = Y, C−3 = Z).

NOTE

• Option 1 (ZFXEO) has E and F swapped; Options 3 and 4 end in Q, which would need R+1, so the shift is inconsistent.

• Forward/backward shift codes always use the same fixed number for every letter; always test the second letter too.

question: In a certain code language, "HUNTERS" is written as " TSFUOVI." How will "FARMERS" be written?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. TSFNSBG.

GIVEN

• HUNTERS → TSFUOVI; find the code of FARMERS.

SOLUTION

• Reverse HUNTERS: S R E T N U H.

• Add +1 to each letter: S→T, R→S, E→F, T→U, N→O, U→V, H→I = TSFUOVI ✓.

• Rule: reverse the word, then move every letter 1 step forward.

• FARMERS reversed: S R E M R A F.

• +1 each: S→T, R→S, E→F, M→N, R→S, A→B, F→G.

• Code = TSFNSBG.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Code with the same number of letters but a mirrored pattern means "reverse + shift". Check the last letter of the word with the first letter of the code (S → T).

NOTE

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are wrong because every letter must be reversed and then moved exactly one place forward (S→T, R→S, E→F, M→N, R→S, A→B, F→G); each of these options breaks the rule at one or more letters (e.g., Option 2 starts TR…, but R is not S+1).

question:
Ten years ago, the age of A was twice that of B. Five years hence, the age of C will be three times that of D. Currently, the sum of ages of A and C is 80, and B is 5 years younger than D.

 

Find the present age of A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 16 years.

GIVEN

• (A − 10) = 2 (B − 10); (C + 5) = 3 (D + 5); A + C = 80; B = D − 5 (B is 5 years younger than D).

SOLUTION

• Let B's present age = b. Then A − 10 = 2 (b − 10) ⇒ A = 2b − 10.

• D = b + 5.

• C + 5 = 3 (D + 5) = 3 (b + 10) ⇒ C = 3b + 25.

• A + C = 80 ⇒ (2b − 10) + (3b + 25) = 80 ⇒ 5b + 15 = 80 ⇒ b = 13.

• A = 2 × 13 − 10 = 16 years.

• Check: B = 13, ten years ago A = 6 and B = 3 (6 = 2 × 3 ✓); D = 18, C = 80 − 16 = 64; five years hence C = 69 and D = 23 (69 = 3 × 23 ✓).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Express every age in a single variable (b) and use the sum equation once. Plug-in check from the options: A = 16 gives C = 64, and C + 5 = 69 = 3 × 23 ✓.

NOTE

• Option 1 (12): C = 68, 73 is not divisible by 3. Option 2 (14): C = 66, 71 is not divisible by 3. Option 4 (18): C = 62, 67 is not divisible by 3.

• In the PDF, the key for this question is shown in yellow (correct but not selected); the answer 16 years is the key.

question:
A vessel contains milk and water in the ratio 11 : 4. If 15 litres of water is added, the ratio becomes 11 : 7.

 

What was the initial quantity of milk?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 55 litres.

GIVEN

• Milk : Water = 11 : 4; after adding 15 L water → 11 : 7.

SOLUTION

• Let milk = 11x and water = 4x.

• Milk stays the same: 11x / (4x + 15) = 11 / 7 ⇒ 4x + 15 = 7x ⇒ x = 5.

• Initial milk = 11 × 5 = 55 litres.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Milk part is unchanged (11 = 11), so the water ratio change (7 − 4 = 3 units) = 15 L ⇒ 1 unit = 5 L ⇒ milk = 11 × 5 = 55 L.

NOTE

• Option 1 (44 L) = 11 × 4; Option 3 (66 L) = 11 × 6; Option 4 (77 L) = 11 × 7 (this is just the milk term misread from the 7-part water in the new ratio).

• Whenever one component stays constant in a mixture, equate it directly and find the unit value.

question: Three pipes, A, B and C, can fill a tank in 24 hours, 30 hours and 40 hours, respectively. If all are opened together and pipe C is closed after 8 hours, how much additional time will A and B together take to fill the remaining tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2 hours 40 minutes.

GIVEN

• A = 24 h, B = 30 h, C = 40 h. All open for 8 hours, then C is closed.

SOLUTION

• Take LCM (24, 30, 40) = 120 units as the tank capacity.

• Efficiency: A = 5, B = 4, C = 3 units/hour. A + B + C = 12 units/hour.

• Work done in 8 hours = 12 × 8 = 96 units; remaining = 120 − 96 = 24 units.

• A + B = 9 units/hour ⇒ time = 24 / 9 = 8/3 hours = 2 hours 40 minutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• (1/3 h = 20 minutes) so 8/3 h = 2 h + 2/3 h = 2 h 40 min.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2 h 20 min) = 7/3 h and Option 3 (3 h 12 min) = 16/5 h do not match 24 / 9.

• Option 4 (3 h 40 min) = 11/3 h; this would arise from wrongly using remaining work 33 units.

• The PDF marks Option 2 in yellow as the key; Option 1 appears in red (a wrong selection).

question:
Find the missing number in the following series:

1, 24, 58, 125, 247, 446, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 744.

GIVEN

• Series: 1, 24, 58, 125, 247, 446, ?

SOLUTION

• First differences: 24 − 1 = 23, 58 − 24 = 34, 125 − 58 = 67, 247 − 125 = 122, 446 − 247 = 199.

• Second differences: 34 − 23 = 11, 67 − 34 = 33, 122 − 67 = 55, 199 − 122 = 77.

• The second differences are 11, 33, 55, 77, … (increase by 22 each time), so the next is 99.

• Next first difference = 199 + 99 = 298.

• Missing number = 446 + 298 = 744.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• When the first differences are irregular, take differences of differences. A constant third difference (22) shows a cubic-type series.

NOTE

• Option 1 (724) would need a difference 278; Option 2 (735) a difference 289; Option 4 (774) a difference 328. None of them continues the pattern 11, 33, 55, 77, 99.

question: If in the word TEACHING the first and second letters are interchanged, in the same way the third and fourth, fifth and sixth and so on are interchanged, then what will be the 2nd letter from the right?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. G.

GIVEN

• Word: TEACHING (8 letters); adjacent pairs are interchanged.

SOLUTION

• Pairs: (T, E), (A, C), (H, I), (N, G).

• After interchange: E T C A I H G N → ETCAIHGN.

• Counting from the right: N (1st), G (2nd), H (3rd), I (4th).

• The 2nd letter from the right is G.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• In an even-length word, the last two letters swap. The 2nd letter from the right after swapping is therefore the original 7th letter (here G, from "NG").

NOTE

• Option 1 (I) is the 4th from the right, Option 2 (N) is the 1st from the right, and Option 3 (H) is the 3rd from the right.

• Always rewrite the new word completely before counting positions from the right.

question:
Identify the alternative set of numbers that correctly codes the word. The code uses [Row, Column] format.

What is the correct code for "MARKED"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (4,2)(1,2)(1,5)(3,6)(5,5)(3,2).

GIVEN

• A 6 × 6 letter grid; code format is (Row, Column).

• Word to code: MARKED.

SOLUTION

• M is in Row 4, Column 2 → (4,2).

• A is in Row 1, Column 2 → (1,2).

• R is in Row 1, Column 5 → (1,5).

• K is in Row 3, Column 6 → (3,6).

• E is in Row 5, Column 5 → (5,5) (E also occurs at (1,4); the option decides which coordinate is used).

• D is in Row 3, Column 2 → (3,2).

• Code = (4,2)(1,2)(1,5)(3,6)(5,5)(3,2) → Option 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the distinctive letters first: K occurs only once, at (3,6); only Option 4 has (3,6) in the 4th place with the other letters correct.

NOTE

• Option 1: the 4th code (3,2) is D, not K. Option 2: the 3rd code (1,2) is A, not R. Option 3: the 4th code (2,6) is S, not K, and (5,1) is X, not E.

• In grid questions, some letters appear twice (A at (1,2) and (5,4); R at (1,5) and (5,6); E at (1,4) and (5,5)). Any of those coordinates is acceptable if the option contains a valid one.

question: In a coded blood relation problem: P $Q means P is the mother of Q; P # Q means P is the father of Q; P @ Q means P is the husband of Q; P % Q means P is the sister of Q. If A # B @ C$ D, how is A related to D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Paternal Grandfather.

GIVEN

• $ = mother of, # = father of, @ = husband of, % = sister of.

• A # B @ C $ D.

SOLUTION

• A # B ⇒ A is the father of B.

• B @ C ⇒ B is the husband of C.

• C $ D ⇒ C is the mother of D.

• C is D's mother and B is C's husband ⇒ B is the father of D.

• A is the father of B ⇒ A is the father of D's father = Paternal Grandfather.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Decode each symbol first, then chain: A → father of B → B is D's father ⇒ A is D's father's father.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Father) would need A to be directly the father of D. Option 3 (Great-grandfather) adds one extra generation. Option 4 (Paternal Uncle) would make A the brother of D's father.

• Relations via "father's father" are always called paternal grandfather; "mother's father" is maternal grandfather.

question: Showing a man, a woman said, "He is the grandson of my husband's father, but he is not my son." How is the man related to the woman?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Nephew.

GIVEN

• The man is the grandson of the woman's husband's father (her father-in-law) but not her son.

SOLUTION

• Woman's husband's father = her father-in-law.

• Grandson of her father-in-law = a child of her father-in-law's son or daughter.

• Her own son is excluded, so the man is the son of her husband's brother (or her husband's sister).

• The son of her husband's brother/sister is the woman's nephew.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• "Grandson of my father-in-law, but not my son" ⇒ the man is her husband's nephew, so he is her nephew too.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Son) is ruled out directly by the statement. Option 3 (Brother-in-law) would be a son of her father-in-law, not a grandson. Option 4 (Paternal Uncle) is a generation above.

• The woman's husband's brother's son is the nephew of both the husband and the wife.

question: Select the odd number pair from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 16, 250.

GIVEN

• Pairs: (16, 250), (15, 225), (18, 324), (13, 169).

SOLUTION

• Check whether the second number is the square of the first: 15² = 225 ✓; 18² = 324 ✓; 13² = 169 ✓.

• 16² = 256, not 250 ✗.

• So 16, 250 is the odd one out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Quickly compare the unit digit of the square: 15² ends with 5, 18² ends with 4, 13² ends with 9, but 16² must end with 6, while 250 ends with 0.

NOTE

• Memorize squares up to 30 and cubes up to 15; they are the most common basis for pair/odd-one-out questions in SSC and Railway papers.

question: From the numbered letters of the word 'MONETARY' (1-M, 2-O, 3-N, 4-E, 5-T, 6-A, 7-R, 8-Y), identify the correct sequence that forms the word 'MENTOR'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1 4 3 5 2 7.

GIVEN

• MONETARY: 1-M, 2-O, 3-N, 4-E, 5-T, 6-A, 7-R, 8-Y.

• Target word: MENTOR.

SOLUTION

• M → 1, E → 4, N → 3, T → 5, O → 2, R → 7.

• Sequence = 1 4 3 5 2 7.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the number under each letter of the target word and compare with the options one position at a time; eliminate options by the 3rd position (N = 3).

NOTE

• Option 2 (1 4 3 5 7 2) ends with R, O (MENTRO). Option 3 (1 3 4 5 2 7) gives MNETOR. Option 4 (1 4 5 3 2 7) gives METNOR.

question: Which center code does NOT follow the digit-letter-digit-letter pattern?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. E5F6.

GIVEN

• Required pattern: digit – letter – digit – letter.

SOLUTION

• 1A2B → 1 (digit), A (letter), 2 (digit), B (letter) ✓.

• 3C4D → digit, letter, digit, letter ✓.

• 7G8H → digit, letter, digit, letter ✓.

• E5F6 → letter, digit, letter, digit ✗.

• So E5F6 does not follow the pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Look only at the first character; three codes begin with a digit, only one begins with a letter.

NOTE

• In "pattern-based odd one out" questions, mark each character as D (digit) or L (letter) and compare strings: DLDL, DLDL, LDLD, DLDL.

question:
In the given question, a few statements have been given followed by conclusions based on them. Consider the statements to be true and answer which of the given conclusions logically follow the statement.

 

Statements

1. All carnivores are predators.

2. Some predators are endangered.

3. All endangered species are protected.

 

Conclusions

I. Some carnivores are endangered.

II. Some predators are protected.

III. All carnivores are protected.

IV. Some protected species are predators.
option_3: Only I, II and IV follow
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Only II and IV follow.

GIVEN

• All carnivores are predators (A). Some predators are endangered (I). All endangered species are protected (A).

SOLUTION

• I. Some carnivores are endangered – The "some predators" who are endangered may or may not be carnivores. Does not follow.

• II. Some predators are protected – Some predators are endangered and all endangered are protected ⇒ some predators are protected. Follows.

• III. All carnivores are protected – No link between carnivores and endangered species. Does not follow.

• IV. Some protected species are predators – Conversion of II. Follows.

• Only II and IV follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Combine "Some predators are endangered" + "All endangered are protected" (I + A ⇒ I): "Some predators are protected", and its conversion "Some protected are predators".

NOTE

• Option 1 and Option 3 include I or III, which cannot be derived. Option 2 misses the valid conversion IV.

• Remember: I + A → I; A + A → A; A + I → no conclusion (middle term not distributed properly); conversion of "Some" is always valid.

question: If 14#7@2 = 4 and 24#6@3 = 12, then what is the value of 40#5@4?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 32.

GIVEN

• 14 # 7 @ 2 = 4 and 24 # 6 @ 3 = 12.

SOLUTION

• Try # = ÷ and @ = ×.

• 14 ÷ 7 × 2 = 2 × 2 = 4 ✓.

• 24 ÷ 6 × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12 ✓.

• So 40 # 5 @ 4 = 40 ÷ 5 × 4 = 8 × 4 = 32.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Take the first number ÷ second, then × third; the pattern is confirmed by both examples.

NOTE

• Option 1 (30), Option 3 (28), Option 4 (24) do not result from any operation consistent with both examples.

• Apply BODMAS carefully only after the symbols are decoded: ÷ and × have equal rank, so evaluate left to right.

question: If 15 Φ 3 = 10 and 24 Φ 4 = 12, find the value of 35 Φ 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 14.

GIVEN

• 15 Φ 3 = 10 and 24 Φ 4 = 12; find 35 Φ 5.

SOLUTION

• 15 Φ 3: 15 ÷ 3 = 5, and 5 × 2 = 10 ✓.

• 24 Φ 4: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, and 6 × 2 = 12 ✓.

• Rule: a Φ b = (a ÷ b) × 2.

• 35 Φ 5 = (35 ÷ 5) × 2 = 7 × 2 = 14.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Divide the first number by the second and double the result.

NOTE

• Options 2 (12), 3 (16) and 4 (18) do not fit the rule: they would require 35 ÷ 5 = 6, 8 or 9, which is not true.

• The PDF marks Option 1 in yellow (correct but not selected); 14 is the key.

question: If □ = +, ○ = −, Δ = ×, ∇ = ÷, find the value of (12 Δ 4) ∇ 8 ○ 2 □ 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• □ = +, ○ = −, Δ = ×, ∇ = ÷; expression: (12 Δ 4) ∇ 8 ○ 2 □ 5.

SOLUTION

• Substitute the symbols: (12 × 4) ÷ 8 − 2 + 5.

• Brackets first: 12 × 4 = 48.

• Division: 48 ÷ 8 = 6.

• Left to right: 6 − 2 + 5 = 4 + 5 = 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Decode all symbols before calculating, then follow BODMAS (Bracket → Of/Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction); − and + have equal rank, so go left to right.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3) results from 6 − (2 + 5) = −1 ≠ 3; Option 2 (5) and Option 3 (7) arise from wrong grouping or from dropping "+ 5" or "− 2". Only 6 − 2 + 5 = 9 is correct.

question:
In the following question a statement is given followed by some assumptions. Read the assumptions carefully and choose the appropriate option.

Statement:

A school is introducing smart classrooms and investing heavily in digital learning tools. To fund the project, the school intends to reduce certain administrative expenses and apply for grants.

Assumptions:

I. Digital learning tools can enhance students' learning experience.

II. The school has already received the grants.
option_3: Neither I nor II is implicit.
option_4: Both I and II are implicit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only I is implicit..

GIVEN

• Statement: A school is introducing smart classrooms and investing heavily in digital learning tools, planning to reduce certain administrative expenses and apply for grants.

SOLUTION

• Assumption I – Investing heavily in digital tools is only sensible if the school believes they can improve students' learning. Implicit.

• Assumption II – The school "intends to … apply for grants", so the grants are not yet received. This contradicts the statement. Not implicit.

• Hence only I is implicit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• An assumption is implicit if the action in the statement would make no sense without it. Anything that contradicts the statement (like "already received") is never an assumption.

NOTE

• Option 2 and Option 4 wrongly include II. Option 3 ignores the clear link between investment and learning benefit.

• Watch for words such as "already", "all", "only", "never" in assumptions; they are often extreme or contradictory and make the assumption invalid.

question:
Read the given conditions carefully and determine the appropriate outcome for the case provided. If any exception applies, identify the authority to whom the case should be referred.

Criteria for receiving a 50% subsidy on high-yield hybrid seeds:

(i) Must own or lease at least 5 acres of agricultural land.

(ii) Must be a member of the local 'Farmer Producer Organisation' (FPO).

(iii) Must not have received any government agricultural subsidy in the last 2 years.

Exceptions:

Exception (A): If the farmer fails criterion (iii) but was hit by a government-declared drought in the last year, refer the case to the Block Development Officer (BDO).

Exception (B): If the farmer meets all criteria (i), (ii), and (iii) but has an active loan default with a cooperative bank, refer the case to the District Agricultural Credit Committee.

Case: Farmer Harpreet is the owner of 8 acres of land and is an active member of his local FPO. Last year, he received a fertiliser subsidy. His district was officially declared 'drought-hit' by the state government in 2025.
option_2: Case to be referred to the Block Development Officer (BDO)
option_4: Case to be referred to the District Agricultural Credit Committee
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Case to be referred to the Block Development Officer (BDO).

GIVEN

• Three criteria and two exceptions (A and B). Harpreet: 8 acres, active FPO member, received a fertiliser subsidy last year, district declared drought-hit in 2025.

SOLUTION

• Criterion (i): 8 acres ≥ 5 acres ✓.

• Criterion (ii): active FPO member ✓.

• Criterion (iii): received a subsidy last year ✗ (fails).

• Exception (A) applies when the farmer fails (iii) and was hit by a government-declared drought in the last year. His district was officially declared drought-hit in 2025 (last year), so Exception (A) applies.

• Case is to be referred to the Block Development Officer (BDO).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Find which criterion fails first; then check only the exception that begins with that failed criterion.

NOTE

• Option 1 (grant) is wrong since criterion (iii) fails. Option 3 (reject) ignores Exception A. Option 4 refers to the District Agricultural Credit Committee, which is for Exception B (all criteria met plus loan default) – not applicable.

• The PDF marks Option 2 in yellow (correct but not selected); this is the key.

question: You are the CEO of an organisation where an excellent performer has been reported for sexually harassing a junior member of the staff without any physical proof apart from the conflicting statements between the parties involved. On the one hand, according to the principle of zero tolerance, it becomes necessary to immediately suspend the accused pending completion of an investigation into this case. On the other hand, the fact that “an accused person is presumed to be innocent until proven guilty” should not be overlooked. What decision would you take in this situation?
option_1: Terminate the accused immediately to protect the company’s reputation.
option_2: Ignore the claim because there is no hard evidence.
option_3: Suspend accused, investigate independently, and relocate junior staff for safety.
option_4: Mediate between the two and ask them to shake hands.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Suspend accused, investigate independently, and relocate junior staff for safety..

GIVEN

• A high performer is accused of sexual harassment; there is no physical proof, only conflicting statements. Zero tolerance requires suspension; the accused is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

SOLUTION

• A good decision must (a) protect the complainant, (b) give a fair, independent process, and (c) not assume guilt.

• Suspending the accused (as a neutral measure, not a punishment) and holding an independent investigation satisfies both zero tolerance and the presumption of innocence.

• Relocating the junior staff member for safety protects the complainant from any pressure or retaliation during the inquiry.

• Hence Option 3 is the most balanced decision.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• In situational-judgement questions choose the option that is fair, lawful, protects the victim and follows due process. Reject extreme (terminate/ignore) and trivialising (mediate/handshake) options.

NOTE

• Option 1 punishes before proof and violates natural justice. Option 2 ignores a serious complaint and the law. Option 4 trivialises sexual harassment; mediation/"settlement" is not appropriate under the law.

• In India, the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 requires an Internal Committee (IC) to inquire into complaints.

question:
Read the criteria given for a position along with some exceptions and then decide what decision should be taken for the case given.

Criteria for Logistics & Supply Chain Head:

1.MBA in Supply Chain Management with ≥ 60% marks.

2.Age: 30–50 years.

3.Minimum 8 years of industry experience.

Exception: If (1) is not met, but the candidate has 15 years of industry experience and a B.E. degree, refer to ‘CEO’.

Case: Mr. Vijay, 42, has a B.E. degree, 16 years of industry experience, but no MBA. What decision should be taken regarding Vijay?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Refer to CEO..

GIVEN

• Criteria: (1) MBA in SCM with ≥ 60%; (2) age 30–50; (3) ≥ 8 years' experience. Exception: if (1) fails but 15 years' experience and B.E. → refer to CEO.

• Mr. Vijay: age 42, B.E., 16 years' experience, no MBA.

SOLUTION

• Criterion 1: no MBA ✗ (fails).

• Criterion 2: 42 years is within 30–50 ✓.

• Criterion 3: 16 years ≥ 8 years ✓.

• Exception: (1) is not met, but he has 16 years (≥ 15) and a B.E. degree ⇒ the exception applies.

• Decision: Refer to CEO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Only one criterion fails (the one named in the exception). Check the exception's extra conditions (15 years + B.E.); both are met.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Select) is wrong because the failed criterion cannot be ignored. Option 2 (Reject) ignores the exception. Option 4 (Board of Directors) is not the authority named in the exception.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.

Bird : Wing :: Fish : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Fin.

GIVEN

• Bird : Wing :: Fish : ?

SOLUTION

• A bird uses its wing as the organ for flying (movement through air).

• A fish uses its fin as the organ for swimming (movement through water).

• So the answer is Fin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Frame the relation in one sentence ("a bird moves with its wing") and apply it to the third word ("a fish moves with its fin").

NOTE

• Option 1 (Water) is the habitat, not an organ. Option 3 (Gill) is the organ of respiration, not movement (the red mark in the PDF shows this was a common wrong choice). Option 4 (Tail) also helps in swimming, but a fin is the main organ of locomotion, as the wing is for a bird.

• The PDF marks Option 2 in yellow as the key.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.

Spoke : Wheel :: Rung : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ladder.

GIVEN

• Spoke : Wheel :: Rung : ?

SOLUTION

• A spoke is a part of a wheel.

• A rung is a step (a crosspiece) that is part of a ladder.

• Relation: part : whole ⇒ Ladder.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Identify the relation first (part – whole) and then pick the whole that contains the third word as a component.

NOTE

• Chair, bed and table have legs, not rungs. (A chair can have rungs between its legs, but the standard "rung" is a ladder's step, and Ladder is the best-fitting answer.)

question:
Read the criteria given for a position along with some exceptions and then decide what decision should be taken for the case given.

The following are the requirements for recruiting in PowerGrid Fabricators, Delhi:

A. At least 75% in class 10th AND 12th.

B. At least 70% in Mechanical or Civil Engineering.

C. Age not more than 25 years as on October 09, 2017.

D. At least 60% in selection test.

E. CAD course from a reputed institute.

Exception 1: Fails only C + more than 1 year experience at a reputed company → Refer to Managing Director.

Exception 2: Fails only E + willing to pay ₹35,000 or more + at least 75% in graduation → Refer to Chairman.

Case: Vikram scored 82% in class 10th and 75% in class 12th. He graduated with 76% in Mechanical Engineering. He scored 58% in the selection test. He has NOT done a CAD course but is ready to pay ₹40,000. He was born on 30/09/1992 and has 2 years of experience at Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. (BHEL). What will be decided in his case?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Candidate is not selected..

GIVEN

• Requirements A–E and Exceptions 1 and 2 (each applies only if that single criterion alone is failed).

• Vikram: 82% (10th), 75% (12th); 76% in Mechanical Engineering; 58% in the selection test; no CAD course (ready to pay ₹40,000); born 30/09/1992; 2 years' experience at BHEL.

SOLUTION

• A: 82% and 75% are both ≥ 75% ✓.

• B: 76% in Mechanical Engineering ≥ 70% ✓.

• C: On 09 October 2017 he is 25 years and 9 days old (born 30/09/1992) – more than 25 years ✗ (fails).

• D: 58% < 60% ✗ (fails).

• E: No CAD course ✗ (fails).

• He fails C, D and E – three criteria. Exception 1 needs "fails only C" and Exception 2 needs "fails only E", so neither applies.

• Decision: Candidate is not selected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Count the failed criteria. If more than one fails, the "fails only …" exceptions can never apply, so the candidate is rejected without checking the extra conditions (experience/fee).

NOTE

• Option 1 and Option 2 are traps built from the experience (2 years) and the ₹40,000 payment, but they need the candidate to fail only C or only E. Option 3 ignores the failed criteria.

• Age check: 30/09/1992 → 30/09/2017 = exactly 25 years; 09/10/2017 is 9 days beyond that, so he exceeds the age limit.

question:
Read the given statement carefully and the following assumptions based on it. Decide which of the assumptions are implicit in the statement.

Statement:

Educational institutions should require at least two hours of daily physical activity for students to promote balanced mental and physical development.

Assumptions:

I. Regular physical exercise is essential for the balanced growth and development of children.

II. Students currently do not engage in sufficient physical activity during their school hours.
option_3: Both Assumptions I and II are implicit
option_4: Neither Assumption I nor II is implicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both Assumptions I and II are implicit.

GIVEN

• Statement: Institutions should require at least two hours of daily physical activity to promote balanced mental and physical development.

SOLUTION

• Assumption I – The statement recommends physical activity "to promote balanced development", so the author assumes that regular exercise helps (is essential for) balanced growth. Implicit.

• Assumption II – A rule is suggested because the present arrangement is felt to be inadequate; if students were already getting enough activity, there would be no need to "require" two hours. Implicit.

• Hence both I and II are implicit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Ask two questions: (1) Why is the action recommended? (the purpose ⇒ Assumption I); (2) Why is the action needed now? (the problem ⇒ Assumption II).

NOTE

• Option 1 and Option 2 each accept only one of the two valid links. Option 4 rejects both and ignores the purpose and need in the statement.

• The PDF marks Option 3 in yellow (correct but not selected); this is the key. Option 1 was selected and is shown in red. Assumption II is somewhat debatable (it is an inference of need), but it is the answer given in the PDF.

question: Through which pass does the river Sutlej enter India from Tibet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shipki La.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Shipki La.

 

• The Sutlej (Satadru in Vedic times) rises near Rakshastal Lake (Mansarovar region) in Tibet and enters India through Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh (Kinnaur district) (हिमाचल प्रदेश).

 

• It is a tributary of the Indus, flows through Himachal Pradesh and Punjab, and meets the Chenab at Uch Sharif in Pakistan (Panjnad), which joins the Indus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shipki La is a border pass on the India–China (Tibet) border and carries the Hindustan–Tibet road (NH-5); it is also a trade route.

 

• Dams on the Sutlej: Bhakra (Gobind Sagar), Nathpa Jhakri, Karcham Wangtoo, Kol Dam.

 

• The Sutlej is the longest of the five rivers of Punjab (Indian part ≈ 1,050 km).

 

NOTE

 

• Nathu La (Sikkim) connects Sikkim and Tibet; the Teesta basin is nearby (not the Sutlej).

 

• Lipulekh (Uttarakhand) is the route to Kailash Mansarovar and is located on the India–Nepal–China tri-junction.

 

• Zoji La (Jammu & Kashmir/Ladakh) lies between Srinagar and Kargil/Leh; it is a mountain pass within India.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: Which Indian state is the largest producer of jowar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Millets: Jowar (sorghum), Bajra (pearl millet; Rajasthan is the leading producer), Ragi (finger millet; Karnataka is the leading producer).

• Jowar is the staple food of people in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka (bhakri/roti).

 

NOTE

• Gujarat leads in cotton and groundnut; its jowar production is much smaller.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

question: Which statement correctly describes the Earth's geoid shape?
option_1: Geoid remains identical to the topographic surface.
option_2: Geoid assumes a perfect geometric sphere shape.
option_3: Geoid varies based on atmospheric wind patterns.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Geoid reflects global gravity variations..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Geoid reflects global gravity variations.

 

• The geoid is the equipotential surface of Earth's gravity field that coincides with mean sea level (extended under the continents). It is irregular because the density of Earth's interior is not uniform, so gravity varies from place to place (भू-आभ).

 

• The geoid is slightly bumpy (undulations of about −100 m to +80 m relative to the reference ellipsoid) and is the true shape of the Earth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Earth is an oblate spheroid (flattened at the poles, bulging at the equator) – not a perfect sphere.

 

• Gravity is stronger at the poles (about 9.83 m/s²) and weaker at the equator (about 9.78 m/s²).

 

• The geoid is used as the reference for measuring heights above sea level; GRACE and GOCE satellites map it.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is wrong because the topographic surface (mountains, valleys) differs from the smooth geoid.

 

• Option 2 is wrong because the geoid is not a perfect sphere (it is an irregular spheroid).

 

• Option 3 is wrong because atmospheric winds do not determine the geoid; it depends on the gravity field.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option:

1. Before Permanent Settlement 1793, zamindars had only the right to collect revenue.

2. After Permanent Settlement 1793, peasants became the legal owners of land.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 is correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Only 1 is correct.

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Before 1793 the zamindars were essentially hereditary revenue collectors (they collected land revenue from the peasants for the state and kept a share), and the land belonged to neither the zamindar nor the peasant in the modern ownership sense.

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: The Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) of 1793 was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. It made the zamindars the legal owners of the land; the peasants (ryots) became tenants and lost their traditional rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the Permanent Settlement, the revenue was fixed permanently (about 10/11 for the Company and 1/11 for the zamindar), and failure to pay on the "sunset" date led to the auction of the estate (Sunset Law).

 

• It was also known as the Zamindari/Istamrari Bandobast and covered about 19% of British India.

 

• Other systems: Ryotwari (Madras and Bombay; Thomas Munro) and Mahalwari (North-West Provinces; Holt Mackenzie / R. M. Bird).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 and Option 3 are wrong because they claim peasants became the owners; ownership went to the zamindars.

 

• Option 4 is wrong because statement 1 is correct.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

question:

• Under this system the government settled revenue directly with the ryot (cultivator), who was recognised as the owner; the rate was typically 30–55% of the produce, and it was revised every 20–30 years.

 

• It covered about 51% of British India (Madras, Bombay, Assam and parts of Coorg).

 

• The system is also known as the Munro system.

question: Which group of athletes is required to file whereabouts information as part of anti-doping regulations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Registered Testing Pool (RTP).

• The correct answer is Registered Testing Pool (RTP).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• WADA was established in 1999 (HQ: Montreal, Canada); NADA India is India's national anti-doping agency (est. 2009).

• "Junior Athletes (JUN)", "Retired Athletes (RET)" and "National Athletes (NAT)" are not the categories used for whereabouts filing; only athletes placed in a testing pool (RTP) have to file whereabouts.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3. (The PDF key is Option 3, in yellow; the selected Option 4 is in red.)

question: The defect of vision caused by ageing and weakening of ciliary muscles is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Presbyopia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Presbyopia.

 

• Presbyopia (जरा-दूरदृष्टिता) is the age-related loss of the ability of the eye to focus on near objects. With age, the ciliary muscles weaken and the eye lens loses its flexibility, so the near point moves farther away (usually after about 40–45 years).

 

• It is corrected using bifocal lenses (concave on top for distance, convex at the bottom for reading) or progressive/reading glasses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Myopia (near-sightedness): distant objects are blurred; the image forms in front of the retina; corrected by a concave lens.

 

• Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): near objects are blurred; the image forms behind the retina; corrected by a convex lens.

 

• Astigmatism: uneven curvature of the cornea; corrected by a cylindrical lens.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Myopia) and Option 2 (Hypermetropia) are not due to age; they occur from the eyeball's length or the lens's power.

 

• Option 4 (Cataract) is clouding (opacity) of the eye lens, causing blurred vision; the treatment is surgery. (The red mark in the PDF shows that this was a common wrong choice.)

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

question: Why did Hershey and Chase use radioactive phosphorus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To label viral DNA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is To label viral DNA.

 

• In the Hershey–Chase experiment (1952), Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase used the T2 bacteriophage (a virus that infects *E. coli*). They grew one batch of phages in radioactive phosphorus (³²P), which gets incorporated in the DNA (DNA contains phosphorus; proteins do not), and another batch in radioactive sulphur (³⁵S), which labels the protein coat (proteins contain sulphur; DNA does not).

 

• After infection and blending, the ³²P was found inside the bacterial cells and the ³⁵S stayed outside. This proved that DNA, not protein, is the genetic material (आनुवंशिक पदार्थ).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hershey and Chase shared the 1969 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (shared with Max Delbrück and Salvador Luria, for discoveries on the replication and genetic structure of viruses; Martha Chase was not a recipient).

 

• Earlier evidence: Griffith's transformation experiment (1928) and Avery, MacLeod and McCarty (1944).

 

• DNA is a polymer of nucleotides joined by phosphodiester bonds (the phosphate group contains phosphorus).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is wrong because the protein coat was labelled with sulphur (³⁵S), not phosphorus.

 

• Option 2 is wrong because the bacterial DNA was not labelled; the viral DNA entered the bacteria.

 

• Option 4 is wrong because RNA was not the subject of this experiment. (The PDF marks Option 3 in yellow as the key; Option 2 appears in red as a wrong selection.)

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

question: The New Development Bank, established by BRICS - originally Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa - differs from the Bretton Woods institutions, mainly the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, because it:

option_4: was designed to reflect greater equality among emerging economies
solution_text:

• The New Development Bank (NDB), also called the BRICS Bank, was established to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in BRICS and other emerging economies (EMDCs). Additional Information

 

• The agreement to set up the NDB was signed at the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza (Brazil), 2014; the bank started operations in 2015 and its headquarters is Shanghai, China.

 

• Its first President was K. V. Kamath (India); Dilma Rousseff (Brazil's former president) has been President since 2023.

 

• The Bretton Woods institutions (IMF and World Bank) were created at the Bretton Woods Conference (1944); the IMF is headquartered in Washington, D.C.

 

• BRICS also created the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) as a financial safety net.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 is wrong because the NDB is an independent multilateral development bank, not under UN control.

 

• Option 3 is wrong because the NDB has no military-development mandate.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

question: A obtains B’s consent for a dangerous procedure by falsely telling B that it is a harmless medical test. B agrees, believing the statement. During the procedure, B suffers injury. Which of the following is correct under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
option_1: Consent is valid because B expressly agreed.
option_2: Consent is invalid because it was obtained under a misconception of fact.
option_3: Consent is valid unless B is under twelve years of age.
option_4: Consent becomes invalid only if grievous hurt occurs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Consent is invalid because it was obtained under a misconception of fact..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Consent is invalid because it was obtained under a misconception of fact.

 

• Under Section 28 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 (corresponding to Section 90 of the old IPC), a consent is not a valid consent if it is given by a person under fear of injury or under a misconception of fact, and the person doing the act knows, or has reason to believe, that the consent was given in consequence of such fear or misconception (सहमति).

 

• Here A falsely told B that the procedure was harmless; B's consent was based on that false belief. Therefore, B's consent is invalid, and A can be held liable for the injury caused (for example, for hurt).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Section 28 also treats consent as invalid if given by a person of unsound mind or intoxicated (unable to understand the nature and consequence), or by a child under twelve years of age (unless the contrary appears from the context).

 

• BNS 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (with BNSS replacing the CrPC and BSA replacing the Evidence Act); these came into force on 1 July 2024.

 

• BNS has 358 sections (IPC had 511).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is wrong because express agreement is not enough when it comes from a misconception. Option 3 is wrong because the age rule is only one of the grounds. Option 4 is wrong because invalidity depends on how the consent was obtained, not on whether grievous hurt occurs.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: As per Census 2011, which state recorded the highest total workforce participation rate (combined)?

question: In May 2026, the newly discovered evergreen tree species “Humboldtia nairiana” was found in which of the following protected areas?

It is endemic to Kerala and was found in the Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuary, part of the Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve, at about 300 m elevation.

 

• The species is extremely rare: fewer than 10 mature trees were reported in a habitat of under 2 sq. km, so it is a candidate for a threatened category. The name honours Prof. G. M. Nair.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

• Genus *Humboldtia* is endemic to the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka.

 

NOTE

question: Which combustion cycle does ISRO's SCE-200 Semicryogenic Engine employ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oxidizer rich Staged Combustion Cycle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Oxidizer rich Staged Combustion Cycle.

 

• The SCE-200 is ISRO's semi-cryogenic engine being developed by the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC). It uses liquid oxygen (LOX) and refined kerosene (RP-1 grade) and a closed-loop oxidizer-rich staged combustion cycle, with a thrust of about 2,000 kN (200 tonnes).

 

• In this cycle all the oxidizer first passes through a pre-burner with a small amount of fuel, and the hot, oxygen-rich gas then drives the turbine before entering the main combustion chamber, giving a higher specific impulse (अर्ध-क्रायोजेनिक इंजन).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The semi-cryogenic engine will be used in the LVM3 upgrade and future launch vehicles, e.g., the Unified Launch Vehicle, to increase payload capacity.

 

• Vikas is ISRO's liquid-fuel engine (UH25 + N₂O₄, gas generator cycle); CE-20 is the cryogenic engine (LH₂ + LOX, gas generator cycle).

 

• Cryogenic engines use fuels at extremely low temperatures; semi-cryogenic engines use cryogenic oxidizer (LOX) but non-cryogenic fuel (kerosene).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Gas Generator) is the cycle used in the Vikas and CE-20 engines. Option 2 (Closed Expander) is used in engines such as RL10 and is not the cycle of SCE-200 (ISRO's CE-7.5 uses a staged combustion cycle). Option 4 (Pressure fed) is a low-performance cycle used in small thrusters.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

question: Which material was primarily used for sculptures produced by the Mathura School of Art?
option_1: Grey schist stone quarried from mountains
option_3: Mud and stucco over wooden frames

• The Mathura School of Art (flourished from about the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE, especially under the Kushanas) is an indigenous school of Indian sculpture. Its sculptures were made mainly from spotted red sandstone (from the Sikri/Karauli region) (मथुरा कला शैली).

 

• It is known for Buddha, Jain Tirthankara and Hindu deity images, the Kanishka headless statue, Yakshi figures and a focus on spiritual expression, a strong body form and a smiling face.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gandhara School (Greco-Roman influence) used grey/blue-grey schist and stucco; it shows realistic anatomy, wavy hair and drapery.

 

• The Amaravati School (Satavahana, Andhra) used white marble / limestone (Palnad marble).

 

• Mathura is credited with some of the earliest images of the Buddha in human form in a purely Indian style; the Kushana rulers patronised both Mathura and Gandhara.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (grey schist) describes the Gandhara School – it appears in red in the PDF as a wrong selection. Option 3 (mud and stucco on wooden frames) is not the primary material of Mathura sculpture. Option 4 (white marble from coastal rivers) does not describe Mathura art; Amaravati used a whitish-green limestone.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: Which mathematical transformation is applied to Gross National Income (GNI) per capita while calculating the income dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI) to account for diminishing returns to income?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Logarithmic transformation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Logarithmic transformation.

 

• In the Human Development Index (HDI) of the UNDP, the income dimension (standard of living) is measured by GNI per capita (PPP $), and the natural logarithm of this value is used. The logarithm shows that each additional dollar of income gives less human-development benefit at higher incomes (diminishing returns) (मानव विकास सूचकांक).

 

• HDI = geometric mean of three dimension indices: Health (life expectancy at birth), Education (mean and expected years of schooling) and Income (log of GNI per capita).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• HDI was introduced in 1990 by Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen; the UNDP publishes the Human Development Report every year.

 

• HDI value ranges from 0 to 1; since 2010 the geometric mean is used. Goalposts for GNI per capita: minimum $100 and maximum $75,000.

 

• Related indices: Gender Development Index (GDI), Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), Inequality-adjusted HDI.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (exponential) would increase the effect of high incomes, which is the opposite of diminishing returns. Option 3 (linear) treats every rupee/dollar equally; it appears in red in the PDF as a wrong selection. Option 4 (square) is not used in the HDI.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: Which policy instrument was dismantled under the trade reforms introduced in India in 1991 to promote competitiveness and efficiency?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Quantitative restrictions on imports.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Quantitative restrictions on imports.

 

• The 1991 trade policy reforms (part of the LPG – Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation reforms, introduced under PM P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh) dismantled quantitative restrictions (import licensing and quotas) on imports of most manufactured consumer goods and capital goods, and reduced tariffs sharply. The aim was to improve competitiveness and efficiency (मात्रात्मक प्रतिबंध).

 

• Quantitative restrictions were also gradually removed on the rest of the goods by 2001 (as per WTO commitments).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other 1991 reforms: devaluation of the rupee (July 1991), the abolition of industrial licensing (except for a few industries), reduction of the public-sector reserved list (from 17 to 8 industries), and permission for 51% FDI in priority industries.

 

• The New Economic Policy (NEP) 1991 was triggered by the balance-of-payments crisis.

 

• The Foreign Trade Policy (earlier EXIM policy) and Special Economic Zones (SEZs) act on trade after 1991.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (canalisation) was reduced, but the key liberalisation measure was the removal of import licensing/quantitative restrictions as given in the PDF. Option 3 (export promotion schemes) were retained and rationalised; Option 4 (import duty concessions) are not what was dismantled.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: A 2 kg (kilogram) object moving at 6 m/s (meters per second) comes into contact with an initially uncompressed spring and compresses it by 0.20 m(meters) before momentarily coming to rest. Assuming that there are no energy losses, what is the spring constant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1800 (newtons per meter).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is 1800 (newtons per meter).

 

• With no energy loss, the kinetic energy of the object = elastic potential energy stored in the spring: ½ m v² = ½ k x².

 

• ½ × 2 × (6)² = ½ × k × (0.20)² ⇒ 36 = 0.02 k ⇒ k = 1800 N/m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hooke's law: F = −kx; the SI unit of the spring constant k is N/m.

 

• Elastic potential energy of a spring: U = ½ k x²; kinetic energy: K = ½ m v².

 

• The mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) stays constant in a conservative system (law of conservation of energy).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2 (280), 3 (720) and 4 (360) do not satisfy ½mv² = ½kx². Common slips are using mv² instead of ½mv² (gives k = 3600) or forgetting to square x.

 

• The PDF marks Option 1 in yellow as the key.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

question: Why is economics commonly described as the study of choice?
option_1: Because individuals always make perfectly rational decisions
option_2: Because scarce resources must be allocated among competing uses
option_3: Because governments determine every economic activity
option_4: Because producers completely determine consumer preferences
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because scarce resources must be allocated among competing uses.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct answer is Because scarce resources must be allocated among competing uses.

 

• Economics deals with the problem of scarcity: human wants are unlimited but resources (land, labour, capital) are limited and have alternative uses. Because of this, people, firms and governments must choose how to use them – so economics is the "study of choice" (चयन का अध्ययन).

 

• Every choice involves an opportunity cost – the value of the next best alternative given up.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lionel Robbins' definition (1932): "Economics is a science which studies human behaviour as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses."

 

• Adam Smith (Wealth definition), Alfred Marshall (Welfare definition), Paul Samuelson (Growth definition).

 

• Central problems of every economy: what to produce, how to produce, for whom to produce.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is wrong because people are not always perfectly rational. Option 3 is wrong because governments do not decide every activity in a market economy. Option 4 is wrong because consumers' preferences are not completely determined by producers.

 

• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: Find the smallest number which is a perfect square and is divisible by 6, 10, 15, and 30.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 900.

GIVEN

• The number must be divisible by 6, 10, 15 and 30, and must be a perfect square.

SOLUTION

• LCM of 6, 10, 15, 30: 6 = 2 × 3; 10 = 2 × 5; 15 = 3 × 5; 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 ⇒ LCM = 30.

• The number must be a multiple of 30, i.e., 2 × 3 × 5 × k.

• For a perfect square, every prime must occur an even number of times: multiply by 2 × 3 × 5 = 30 again.

• Smallest number = 30 × 30 = 900 (= 30²).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• If the LCM is a product of distinct primes (square-free), then the smallest perfect square divisible by it is LCM²: 30² = 900.

NOTE

• Option 1 (400) is not divisible by 3. Option 3 (2500) is not divisible by 3. Option 4 (1600) is not divisible by 3. Only 900 is divisible by 30 (900 ÷ 30 = 30).

question: The ratio of juice and water in a mixture is 2: 3. What is the percentage of juice in the mixture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 40%.

GIVEN

• Juice : Water = 2 : 3.

SOLUTION

• Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5.

• Percentage of juice = (2 / 5) × 100 = 40%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Percentage of a part = part ÷ total × 100 (not part ÷ other part).

NOTE

• Option 4 (60%) is the percentage of water (3/5). Option 3 (25%) comes from 1/4 (wrongly dividing by 4 parts). Option 1 (55%) has no basis.

question: A and B invest in a business in the ratio 4:5. After 10 months, B leaves the business after withdrawing his investment. In the first year, the business made a profit of ₹49,000. What is B's share?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹25,000.

GIVEN

• Investments A : B = 4 : 5; B stays for 10 months, A for 12 months; profit = ₹49,000.

SOLUTION

• Profit ratio = (capital × time): A : B = (4 × 12) : (5 × 10) = 48 : 50 = 24 : 25.

• Total parts = 24 + 25 = 49.

• B's share = (25 / 49) × 49,000 = ₹25,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The total ratio (49) equals the thousands in the profit (49,000), so each part = ₹1,000; B = 25 parts = ₹25,000.

NOTE

• Option 3 (₹24,000) is A's share. Option 2 (₹20,000) and Option 4 (₹22,000) come from ignoring time or using the wrong ratio (e.g., 4 : 5 gives B = ₹27,222).

• Profit sharing rule: Ratio = Investment × Time.

question: In an innings of 108 runs, a batsman hit 9 boundaries and 3 sixes. Find the percentage of runs scored by running.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 50%.

GIVEN

• Total runs = 108; boundaries = 9 (4 runs each); sixes = 3 (6 runs each).

SOLUTION

• Runs from boundaries = 9 × 4 = 36.

• Runs from sixes = 3 × 6 = 18.

• Runs scored by hitting = 36 + 18 = 54.

• Runs by running = 108 − 54 = 54.

• Percentage = (54 / 108) × 100 = 50%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Boundary-and-six runs = 54, exactly half of 108, so 50% is the answer straightaway.

NOTE

• Option 3 (32%) is close to the share of runs from boundaries alone (36/108 ≈ 33%), a trap; Options 2 (65%) and 4 (48%) have no basis in the numbers.

• Runs by running = total − (4 × boundaries) − (6 × sixes).

question: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 61. What is the difference between the highest and lowest numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 8.

GIVEN

• Five consecutive odd numbers with average 61.

SOLUTION

• For consecutive numbers, the average is the middle (3rd) number = 61.

• The numbers: 57, 59, 61, 63, 65.

• Highest − lowest = 65 − 57 = 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For n consecutive odd numbers, difference between highest and lowest = 2 × (n − 1) = 2 × 4 = 8 (average does not matter).

NOTE

• Option 1 (5) and Option 4 (3) are odd numbers, but the difference of two odd numbers is always even. Option 3 (6) is the difference for 4 numbers (2 × 3 = 6).

• The PDF marks Option 2 in yellow as the key.

question: If ₹2,000 amounts to ₹2,315.25 in 3 years at compound interest, what is the rate percent per annum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5%.

GIVEN

• Principal P = ₹2,000; amount A = ₹2,315.25; time = 3 years; compounded annually.

SOLUTION

• A = P (1 + r/100)³ ⇒ 2315.25 / 2000 = (1 + r/100)³.

• 2315.25 / 2000 = 1.157625 = (1.05)³ [1.05 × 1.05 = 1.1025; 1.1025 × 1.05 = 1.157625].

• So 1 + r/100 = 1.05 ⇒ r = 5% per annum.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Test the options: for 5%, amount = 2000 × (21/20)³ = 2000 × 9261/8000 = 2315.25 ✓.

NOTE

• Option 1 (7%): 2000 × 1.07³ = ₹2,450.09. Option 3 (9%): ₹2,590.06. Option 4 (10%): ₹2,662. All give a higher amount than ₹2,315.25.

• Compound interest = A − P = ₹315.25.

question: If a regular polygon has 90 diagonals, what is the measure of each interior angle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 156°.

GIVEN

• Regular polygon with 90 diagonals.

SOLUTION

• Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) / 2 = 90 ⇒ n(n − 3) = 180 ⇒ n² − 3n − 180 = 0.

• (n − 15)(n + 12) = 0 ⇒ n = 15.

• Each exterior angle = 360° / 15 = 24°.

• Each interior angle = 180° − 24° = 156°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Find n by testing: 15 × 12 = 180 (n and n − 3 differ by 3), so n = 15. Interior angle = (n − 2) × 180 / n = 13 × 180 / 15 = 156°.

NOTE

• Option 1 (126°) is not an interior angle of any regular polygon (the exterior angle 54° does not divide 360° evenly); Option 4 (140°) belongs to a 9-sided polygon (exterior 40°, n = 9, diagonals = 27). Option 2 (181°) is greater than 180° and impossible for a regular convex polygon.

• The PDF marks Option 3 in yellow as the key.

question: A sum of ₹15,600 is invested in a scheme of simple interest. The person receives ₹4,680 as interest after 3 years. If he had invested the same sum for 5 years at a rate 2% lower than the original rate, what would be the interest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹6,240.

GIVEN

• P = ₹15,600; SI = ₹4,680 for 3 years. New rate = original − 2%; new time = 5 years.

SOLUTION

• Original rate: R = (SI × 100) / (P × T) = (4,680 × 100) / (15,600 × 3) = 468,000 / 46,800 = 10% p.a.

• New rate = 10% − 2% = 8% p.a.

• New SI = (15,600 × 8 × 5) / 100 = 156 × 40 = ₹6,240.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• ₹4,680 for 3 years ⇒ ₹1,560 per year = 10% of 15,600. At 8%: 1,248 per year × 5 = ₹6,240.

NOTE

• Options 2, 3 and 4 correspond to rates of about 6.9%, 8.33% and 7.5% for 5 years, none of which is 10% − 2% = 8%.

• The PDF marks Option 1 in yellow as the key.

question: If x + 1/x = 2, then what is the value of x⁷ + 1/x¹¹⁷?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• x + 1/x = 2; find x⁷ + 1/x¹¹⁷.

SOLUTION

• x + 1/x = 2 ⇒ x² + 1 = 2x ⇒ (x − 1)² = 0 ⇒ x = 1.

• x⁷ + 1/x¹¹⁷ = 1⁷ + 1/1¹¹⁷ = 1 + 1 = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The only real number whose sum with its reciprocal is 2 is 1 (and −1 gives −2). So any power of x is 1 and the expression is 1 + 1 = 2.

NOTE

• Option 2 (1) results from computing only one term. Options 3 (3) and 4 (4) have no basis.

• Remember: x + 1/x = 2 ⇒ x = 1; x + 1/x = −2 ⇒ x = −1.

• The PDF marks Option 1 in yellow as the key; Option 2 appears in red as a wrong selection.

question: A dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a weight of 960 grams in place of a standard kilogram. Determine the approximate percentage gain achieved by the dealer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 4.17%.

GIVEN

• True weight 1,000 g; false weight used 960 g; sold at cost price.

SOLUTION

• The dealer gives 960 g but charges for 1,000 g, so he keeps (1,000 − 960) = 40 g extra.

• Gain % = (error / (true weight − error)) × 100 = (40 / 960) × 100 = 4.17% (approximately).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Gain % = (True weight − False weight) / False weight × 100 = 40/960 × 100 = 100/24 = 4⅙ % ≈ 4.17%.

NOTE

• Option 1 (5.18%), Option 2 (6.78%) and Option 3 (7.42%) do not match 40/960. A common slip is to divide by 1,000 (giving 4%) instead of the false weight 960.

question: In a circle of radius 42 cm, an arc subtends an angle of 15 degrees at the centre. Find the length of the arc. (Take π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 11 cm.

GIVEN

• Radius r = 42 cm; angle θ = 15°; π = 22/7.

SOLUTION

• Arc length = (θ / 360°) × 2πr = (15 / 360) × 2 × (22/7) × 42.

• 2 × (22/7) × 42 = 264 cm (the circumference).

• Arc = (1/24) × 264 = 11 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 15° is 1/24 of the full circle. Circumference ÷ 24 = 264 ÷ 24 = 11.

NOTE

• Option 3 (22 cm) is the arc for 30°; Option 1 (33 cm) is for 45°; Option 4 (44 cm) is for 60°. In each case the arc is a multiple of 11 cm per 15°.

question: In a circle with center O, AD is a diameter and AC is a chord. Point B is on AD such that OB = 7 cm and BC = 9 cm. If ∠OBC = 60°, find the radius of the circle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. √67 cm.

GIVEN

• O is the centre; C lies on the circle, so OC = radius r. OB = 7 cm, BC = 9 cm, ∠OBC = 60°.

SOLUTION

• In triangle OBC, apply the cosine rule: OC² = OB² + BC² − 2 × OB × BC × cos ∠OBC.

• OC² = 7² + 9² − 2 × 7 × 9 × cos 60° = 49 + 81 − 126 × ½ = 130 − 63 = 67.

• Radius = OC = √67 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Whenever two sides and the included angle are known, use the cosine rule directly: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C.

NOTE

• Options 1 (r² = 256), 2 (r² = 90) and 3 (r² = 625) do not match the cosine-rule value r² = 67.

• The PDF marks Option 4 in yellow as the key. (If ∠OBC were 120° the result would be √193; the 60° angle at B gives √67.)

question: If sin θ + sin³ θ = cos² θ, find the value of cos⁶ θ − 4 cos⁴ θ + 8 cos² θ.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• sin θ + sin³ θ = cos² θ; find cos⁶ θ − 4cos⁴ θ + 8cos² θ.

SOLUTION

• Let s = sin θ. Then cos² θ = 1 − s², and the condition becomes s + s³ = 1 − s², i.e., s³ + s² + s = 1.

• Let c = cos² θ = 1 − s². Then c³ − 4c² + 8c = (1 − s²)³ − 4(1 − s²)² + 8(1 − s²).

• Expand: = 5 − 3s² − s⁴ − s⁶.

• From the condition, s³ = 1 − s − s², so s⁶ = (1 − s − s²)² = 1 − 2s − s² + 2s³ + s⁴, and s⁴ = s − s² − s³.

• Substituting: 5 − 3s² − s⁴ − s⁶ = 4 + 2s − 2s² − 2s³ − 2s⁴ = 4 + 2s − 2s² − 2s³ − 2(s − s² − s³) = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Quick numerical check: s ≈ 0.5437 is the root of s³ + s² + s − 1 = 0, so cos² θ = 1 − s² ≈ 0.7044; then c³ − 4c² + 8c ≈ 0.3495 − 1.9847 + 5.6352 = 4.00.

NOTE

• Option 2 (1), Option 3 (0) and Option 4 (−2) are not obtained from the above algebra or the numerical check (≈ 4.00).

• The PDF marks Option 1 in yellow as the key.

question: If sin A + cos A = √2, determine the value of tan A + cot A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• sin A + cos A = √2.

SOLUTION

• Square both sides: sin² A + cos² A + 2 sin A cos A = 2 ⇒ 1 + 2 sin A cos A = 2 ⇒ sin A cos A = ½.

• tan A + cot A = sin A / cos A + cos A / sin A = (sin² A + cos² A) / (sin A cos A) = 1 / (½) = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• sin A + cos A = √2 occurs only for A = 45°, so tan A + cot A = 1 + 1 = 2.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1/√2) and Option 4 (√2) confuse the answer with sin 45° or the given sum. Option 3 (1/2) is the value of sin A cos A, not tan A + cot A (it appears in red in the PDF as a wrong selection).

• tan A + cot A = 1 / (sin A cos A) = 2 / sin 2A, with a minimum value 2.

The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Expression: [sin 42° sec 48° + cos 42° cosec 48° + tan 38° tan 52°] / [cosec² 31° − tan² 59°].

SOLUTION

• Use complementary angles (42° + 48° = 90°, 38° + 52° = 90°, 31° + 59° = 90°).

• sin 42° sec 48° = sin 42° / cos 48° = sin 42° / sin 42° = 1 (cos 48° = sin 42°).

• cos 42° cosec 48° = cos 42° / sin 48° = cos 42° / cos 42° = 1 (sin 48° = cos 42°).

• tan 38° tan 52° = tan 38° × cot 38° = 1 (tan 52° = cot 38°).

• Numerator = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

• Denominator: tan 59° = cot 31°, so cosec² 31° − cot² 31° = 1.

• Value = 3 / 1 = 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• In such questions, convert every angle to its complement: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ. Each product pairs up to give 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

NOTE

• Option 1 (0), Option 2 (1) and Option 3 (2) result from missing one of the three 1's in the numerator or evaluating the denominator incorrectly.

• Identities to remember: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1; 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ; 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

question: If the radius of a hemisphere is 7 cm, what is the difference between its total surface area and its curved surface area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 154 cm².

GIVEN

• Hemisphere radius r = 7 cm.

SOLUTION

• Curved surface area (CSA) = 2πr².

• Total surface area (TSA) = 3πr² (CSA + the flat circular base πr²).

• Difference = TSA − CSA = 3πr² − 2πr² = πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference = the area of the flat base = πr² = 22 × 7 = 154 cm².

NOTE

• Option 2 (77 cm²) is half of the base area; Option 4 (88 cm²) is not related to the formula; Option 3 (169 cm²) is 13². None of these equals πr².

• Hemisphere formulas: CSA = 2πr², TSA = 3πr², Volume = (2/3)πr³.

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• Expression: (cos³ θ + sin³ θ) / (cos θ + sin θ) + (cos³ θ − sin³ θ) / (cos θ − sin θ).

SOLUTION

• Use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), with a = cos θ, b = sin θ.

• First term: (cos θ + sin θ)(cos² θ − sin θ cos θ + sin² θ) / (cos θ + sin θ) = 1 − sin θ cos θ.

• Second term: (cos θ − sin θ)(cos² θ + sin θ cos θ + sin² θ) / (cos θ − sin θ) = 1 + sin θ cos θ.

• Sum = (1 − sin θ cos θ) + (1 + sin θ cos θ) = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The sum of the two cube-formula results is (1 − p) + (1 + p) = 2, whatever the value of p = sin θ cos θ.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1) would result if only one term is considered; Option 2 (0) arises from subtracting the terms; Option 4 (−2) has no basis. (In the PDF, Option 2 appears in red as a wrong selection; Option 3 in yellow is the key.)

question: In a circle with a diameter of 34 cm, two parallel chords are drawn on opposite sides of the center. The length of one chord is 30 cm, and the perpendicular distance between the two chords is 23 cm. Calculate the length of the other chord.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 16 cm.

GIVEN

• Diameter = 34 cm ⇒ radius r = 17 cm. One chord = 30 cm; distance between the parallel chords = 23 cm; the chords are on opposite sides of the centre.

SOLUTION

• The perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord. For the 30 cm chord: half = 15 cm; distance from centre d₁ = √(17² − 15²) = √(289 − 225) = √64 = 8 cm.

• Chords lie on opposite sides: d₁ + d₂ = 23 ⇒ d₂ = 23 − 8 = 15 cm.

• Half of the other chord = √(17² − 15²) = √64 = 8 cm.

• Other chord = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Pythagorean triple 8–15–17: a chord of 30 (half 15) is 8 cm from the centre, and a chord at 15 cm from the centre has half-length 8, i.e., length 16.

NOTE

• Options 1 (14), 3 (20) and 4 (24) do not satisfy d₂ = 15 with r = 17 (e.g., a chord of 24 would be √(289 − 144) = √145 from the centre).

• Formula: half chord² = r² − (distance from centre)².

question: A square pyramid is sliced by a plane parallel to its base at a point that is one-third of the way down from the apex along its height. If the volume of the original pyramid is 540 cm³, determine the volume of the resulting frustum.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 520 cm³.

GIVEN

• Original pyramid volume = 540 cm³. The cut is made at 1/3 of the height from the apex, parallel to the base.

SOLUTION

• The small pyramid cut off at the top is similar to the original, with height ratio 1 : 3.

• Volume ratio = (1/3)³ = 1/27.

• Volume of small pyramid = 540 / 27 = 20 cm³.

• Volume of frustum = 540 − 20 = 520 cm³.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• For similar solids, volume ∝ (linear ratio)³. The top is 1/27 of the whole, so the frustum is 26/27 × 540 = 520 cm³.

NOTE

• Option 2 (578) is greater than the original volume, so it is impossible. Option 1 (415) and Option 4 (480) correspond to cut fractions that do not match 1/27 (540 − 415 = 125, 540 − 480 = 60).

• The PDF marks Option 3 in yellow as the key; Option 1 appears in red as a wrong selection.

question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 19% on the cost price of an article after giving three consecutive discounts of 11%, 13% and 15% to a customer. What would have been the profit percentage, had the shopkeeper given discounts of 11% and 13% only?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 40%.

GIVEN

• Three discounts 11%, 13%, 15% give a profit of 19%. Find the profit % if only 11% and 13% are given.

SOLUTION

• Let the marked price (MP) = 100.

• After 11% and 13%: SP₂ = 100 × 0.89 × 0.87 = 77.43.

• After the third discount of 15%: SP₃ = 77.43 × 0.85 = 65.8155.

• SP₃ gives a 19% profit: CP = 65.8155 / 1.19 = 55.3071.

• Required profit % = (77.43 − 55.3071) / 55.3071 × 100 = 40%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Both selling prices have the same cost price, and SP₂ = SP₃ / 0.85. So (1 + required profit) = 1.19 / 0.85 = 1.40 ⇒ profit = 40%.

NOTE

• Option 1 (35%), Option 3 (45%) and Option 4 (50%) do not match 1.19 / 0.85 = 1.4.

• The PDF marks Option 2 in yellow as the key.

question: A seller offers a 20% discount and still earns a 25% profit. If the profit made is ₹75, find the marked price of the article.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ₹468.75.

GIVEN

• Discount = 20%; profit = 25% of cost price; profit = ₹75.

SOLUTION

• Profit = 25% of CP = 75 ⇒ CP = 75 / 0.25 = ₹300.

• SP = CP + profit = 300 + 75 = ₹375.

• SP = 80% of MP (after a 20% discount) ⇒ MP = 375 / 0.8 = ₹468.75.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• MP : CP = 125 : 80 = 25 : 16 (SP is 125% of CP and 80% of MP). With CP = 300 ⇒ MP = 300 × 25 / 16 = ₹468.75.

NOTE

• Option 3 (₹490) and Option 4 (₹570) do not follow from CP = ₹300 and a 20% discount; Option 1 (₹504.25) has no basis. A common slip is to take MP = SP = ₹375 or to add 20% to CP, which gives wrong values.

question: The common direct tangent of two circles is 26 cm long, while their common transverse tangent is 10 cm long. Find the product of the radii of the circles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 144.

GIVEN

• Length of the direct common tangent = 26 cm; length of the transverse common tangent = 10 cm. Let the radii be r₁ and r₂ and the distance between the centres d.

SOLUTION

• Direct tangent: L_d² = d² − (r₁ − r₂)² ⇒ 676 = d² − (r₁ − r₂)².

• Transverse tangent: L_t² = d² − (r₁ + r₂)² ⇒ 100 = d² − (r₁ + r₂)².

• Subtract: 676 − 100 = (r₁ + r₂)² − (r₁ − r₂)² = 4 r₁ r₂.

• 576 = 4 r₁ r₂ ⇒ r₁ r₂ = 144.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Product of radii = (L_d² − L_t²) / 4 = (26² − 10²) / 4 = (676 − 100) / 4 = 144.

NOTE

• Options 1 (72), 2 (86) and 3 (100) do not equal (L_d² − L_t²)/4. For instance, forgetting the factor 4 in 4r₁r₂ would give 576, not any of the options.

question: If p + q + r = 0 and  pq + qr + rp = −35, then find p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2450.

GIVEN

• p + q + r = 0 and pq + qr + rp = −35; find p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴.

SOLUTION

• p² + q² + r² = (p + q + r)² − 2(pq + qr + rp) = 0 − 2(−35) = 70.

• p²q² + q²r² + r²p² = (pq + qr + rp)² − 2pqr(p + q + r) = (−35)² − 0 = 1225.

• p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴ = (p² + q² + r²)² − 2(p²q² + q²r² + r²p²) = 70² − 2 × 1225 = 4900 − 2450 = 2450.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When p + q + r = 0: p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴ = (p² + q² + r²)² / 2 = 4900 / 2 = 2450.

NOTE

• Option 4 (4900) is (p² + q² + r²)² without subtracting. Option 1 (2400) and Option 3 (3675) do not follow from the identities (3675 = 3 × 1225 is only the sum for another condition).

• The PDF marks Option 2 in yellow as the key.

question: Tangents PT and PS are drawn from an external point P to a circle of radius 5 cm. If the distance from P to the center O is 13 cm, find the area of quadrilateral PTOS.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 60 cm².

GIVEN

• Radius OT = OS = 5 cm; OP = 13 cm; PT and PS are tangents.

SOLUTION

• A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact: ∠OTP = ∠OSP = 90°.

• In right triangle OTP: PT = √(OP² − OT²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm (also PS = 12 cm).

• Area of triangle OTP = ½ × OT × PT = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

• Quadrilateral PTOS = triangle OTP + triangle OSP = 2 × 30 = 60 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Triplet 5–12–13 gives PT = 12 directly. Area of the kite = 2 × (½ × r × tangent) = r × tangent = 5 × 12 = 60.

NOTE

• Option 1 (30 cm²) is the area of one triangle only. Option 2 (45) and Option 4 (65 = 5 × 13) use wrong lengths.

• Equal tangents from an external point: PT = PS.

• The PDF marks Option 3 in yellow as the key.

question: Plastic and leather are two types of materials used to manufacture industrial washers. How many kg of pure plastic must be added to a mixture of 16 kg of a first washer material and 25 kg of a second washer material to produce a new batch containing exactly 40% leather? The ratio of plastic to leather by weight is 3:1 in the first material and 6:19 in the second material.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 16.5 kg.

GIVEN

• First material: 16 kg, plastic : leather = 3 : 1. Second material: 25 kg, plastic : leather = 6 : 19. Add x kg of pure plastic so that leather = 40% of the new batch.

SOLUTION

• First material: plastic = 16 × 3/4 = 12 kg; leather = 16 × 1/4 = 4 kg.

• Second material: plastic = 25 × 6/25 = 6 kg; leather = 25 × 19/25 = 19 kg.

• Total leather = 4 + 19 = 23 kg (unchanged, since only pure plastic is added); total plastic = 12 + 6 = 18 kg.

• Leather = 40% of the new batch ⇒ new batch weight = 23 / 0.40 = 57.5 kg.

• Weight of the two materials = 16 + 25 = 41 kg ⇒ plastic to be added = 57.5 − 41 = 16.5 kg.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Leather is fixed (23 kg) and must be 40% (2/5) of the total ⇒ total = 57.5 kg. Added plastic = 57.5 − 41 = 16.5.

NOTE

• Check: plastic = 18 + 16.5 = 34.5 kg; 34.5 / 57.5 = 60%, so leather is 40% ✓.

• Option 1 (19.5), Option 2 (18.5) and Option 3 (17.5) would make leather 38.3%, 38.7% and 39.0% respectively, not exactly 40%.

• The PDF marks Option 4 in yellow as the key.

question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

 

The railway department will lay new tracks along the entire route next year.
option_1: New tracks will be being laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.
option_2: New tracks are being laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.
option_3: New tracks will have been laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.
option_4: New tracks will be laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. New tracks will be laid along the entire route by the railway department next year..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the simple future tense (will + base verb): "will lay".

 

• Passive structure of the simple future: Object + will be + V3 + (by + subject).

 

• Object: "new tracks"; verb: "will lay" → "will be laid".

 

• Passive: New tracks will be laid along the entire route by the railway department next year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "will be being laid" is not a valid tense form.

 

• Option 2: "are being laid" is the present continuous passive and does not match "next year".

 

• Option 3: "will have been laid" is the future perfect passive; the original sentence is simple future.

 

NOTE

 

• Tense change in the passive: will + V1 → will be + V3; will have + V3 → will have been + V3; is/are + V1-ing → is/are being + V3.

 

• Verb forms: lay – laid – laid (not to be confused with lie – lay – lain).
